title: A Seedling's Sense of Direction
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript: Put a young bean plant on a windowsill and, within a few days, its stem may lean towards the glass. A teaching lab wanted to know how quickly a plant could respond when the light changed direction. The students grew seedlings under identical lamps and moved half of the lamps to the opposite side of their trays. The other half stayed in place. A camera took a picture every thirty minutes, allowing the class to compare the angle of each stem without touching it. Several moved seedlings began to straighten before leaning the other way, while most of the comparison group continued bending in the original direction. The exercise captured a response to a change in light, but it could not show whether beans grown outdoors would respond at the same speed.

questions.prompt: What did the class want to find out?
options: Which bean variety needed the least light.
How quickly seedlings adjusted to a change in the direction of light.
How far a seedling could bend without breaking.
questions.answer: How quickly seedlings adjusted to a change in the direction of light.
questions.explanation: 实验想了解幼苗在光照方向改变后需要多久才会作出反应。

questions.prompt: What happened to several seedlings after their lamps were moved?
options: Their stems bent further in the original direction.
Their leaves closed before the stems moved.
Their stems began to straighten before bending the other way.
questions.answer: Their stems began to straighten before bending the other way.
questions.explanation: 部分改变光照方向的幼苗先伸直了一些，然后才朝新的方向弯曲。
